newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke says options still open on EMU.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke says options still open on EMU.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke on Sunday denied policy had hardened against the planned European Single Currency and said Britain's option to join remained intact.

In an interview with the BBC, he said he believed it was highly unlikely that EMU would start as scheduled on January 1, 1999 and said the timetable should be delayed if countries could not meet convergence criteria.

"I have always been doubtful about whether we could go ahead on time on January 1, 1999," Clarke said. "I strongly feel that it definitely shouldn't if it means that the convergence hasn't been achieved."

He said he would not rule out Britain joining the single currency and said it was "not impossible" this would happen in 1999, but if countries were not genuinely converging they would be taking risks by going ahead.
"Britain is well placed," Clarke said, "we have a choice that we have placed in our own hands."
